 Word Spud is one of the games released in The Jackbox Party Pack , supporting 2 to 8 players. It's a remaster of its original Flash incarnation .

 Contents

 1 Gameplay 

 2 Achievements 

 3 Promotional art 

 4 Trivia 

 Gameplay [ ] 

 Word Spud begins by giving one player a simple word, such as "real" or "life". The player must then come up with a fitting or witty word or phrase to follow it. During this, the other players may type in their own ideas, which will pop up above their icons. Afterwards, the other players vote on the quality of the entry, giving it a check or an X. Every check is worth one point, and every X takes one away. If the entry received a positive score, that word (or the last word if it was a phrase) becomes the prompt for the next player, and the input appears in the background in the writer's color. Otherwise, the next player is given a new word.

 The number of turns each player gets per round depends on the number of players:

 2 players: 11 turns

 3 players: 7 turns

 4 players: 6 turns

 5 players: 5 turns

 6 players: 4 turns

 7 or 8 players: 3 turns

 At the end, the player with the most points will win the round. The players may then choose to play another, in which case the game will keep track of how many rounds each player has won.

 Achievements [ ] 

 Word Herd 

 – Play a full 8-player game

 Group Hug 

 – Play a perfect round where all words get accepted

 Spud Stud 

 – Win three rounds in a row

 Golden Nugget 

 – Type the word "nugget" and get it accepted

 Promotional art [ ] 

 Trivia [ ] 

 Word Spud is the only game out of The Jackbox Party Packs to not have a host. It is also the only game to not have any music play during the credits.
 Despite having without credits at the end of the game, Steve Heinrich (who also directed YDKJ 2015 and Fibbage XL), directed it and Tim Sniffen (who made art from Fibbage XL) made the art.

 In the official trailer for “The Jackbox Party Pack 7,” there’s a mug that says “WORD’S BEST SPUD,” with the logo for Word Spud sprinted on.

 The game, along with Zeeple Dome is often ridiculed as the worst game in a Jackbox Party Pack. In turn, Jackbox Games has poked fun at Word Spud in other Party Pack games and even Word Spud's page on their website.
 In Drawful 2, a player get an achievement by entering word spud 2 as decoy.

 In Quiplash XL , Schmitty will react on the prompt "An angry review you'd give this game (Quiplash)" if someone says that it's not as good as Word Spud.

 In Trivia Murder Party, when someone escaped. A newspaper subtitle will sometimes show: “Word Spud 2 delayed.”

 In Survive the Internet , Word Spud 2 shows up as both a pop-up ad and a background application.

 During a commercial of You Don't Know Jack Full Stream Mike Bilder mentions Word Spud 3 as a potential next game.

 Word Spud is referenced in Push The Button , where the host D.O.D.E. sometimes says "In order to run this test, I've deleted Word Spud from the database."

 In the lead up to announcing Drawful Animate , Jackbox Games released a series of teaser GIF's on their Twitter account with phrases written on them. The blacked out letters from each post spell out Word Spud Two .

 In Drawful Animate, word spud 2 is one of the in-game provided decoys, if a player enters nothing or the input got rejected by the moderator.

 In the game The Wheel of Enormous Proportions, Word Spud is one of the possible answers of the wheel.
 More specifically to the question "What's the meaning of life?", in which it will answer "The answer to life is Jackbox Games’ Word Spud . No, I was not paid to say that."

 In Quixort on the prompt "Jackbox Party Pack Games", Word Spud appears as an answer.

 On the Pack 10 start menu a potato is placed on a shelf near the stack of Party Pack 1 games.
 In addition, in one of the idle animation easter eggs on the start menu, a Word Spud screensaver appear on Jerri's computer.

 According to the website, Word Spud 2 will release in 3145, this is however a joke because it's a playful way of saying there are no plans for a sequel.

 The fonts used are Courier New, Effra Medium, Effra Light & TVNordEFOP-Heavy.

 Word Spud (stylized as WORD SPUD ) is a word association party video game and one of five games featured in The Jackbox Party Pack .

 Gameplay

 One player is randomly selected and presented with a randomly selected "prefix" (like "light-" or "super-," for example,) and they have to form a full word or sentence with it ("lighthouse" or "super great",) then everyone else votes on it, whether giving a YES or a NO. Points are added for the players voting for YES, and are subtracted for players voting NO. 

 If a majority of people vote for "YES," then the addition to the word that the previous player is given to the next randomly selected player (in this case, "house" and "great" would be sent to the next player;) however, if the majority votes "NO," then a new prefix is presented to the next player.

 This cycle continues until the timer at the top ends. At which point, the player/s with the most points will earn a star and will be presented with the option of going to the next round or ending the game.

 Development

 Word Spud originally started as a Flash game in 2004 as an open beta by Jellyvision , then released in 2006. The game only supported 4 players, including adding or removing bots into the game, and the rules stayed the same. You could also adjust the amount of words, the speed of the words, and the amount of minutes in total. [ citation needed ] 

 The original game was also accompanied with a song, which was once revealed at the start of a Party Pack 1 Word Spud stream on their official Twitch account, which was archived on their YouTube in 2014. [ 1 ] The lyrics went like this:

 When a word is passed to your name... 

 Type a word or a phrase that relates to it. 

 And then you hit Return, then the other players vote 

 And if they like what you say, then you'll feel so gay 

 Cuz you just made a Wordspud, hey! 

 Word Spud! 

 Trivia

 This is one of only two Jackbox games to have no host, the other being Hear Say .

 This is the only Jackbox game to not display the credits at the end of the game—the credits however are located in the game's files.

 This game is frequently joked about with having a sequel, as even the official site states that its sequel is "coming in the year 3145!" [ 2 ]
